title: Extended-Factor-Graph SASCA for Masked Multiplication
summary: Per-measurement SASCA belief propagation tends to degrade as noise rises; it remains open how the extended-factor-graph variant performs and whether its gain over standard DPA is noise-independent.

formal_statement.body: For $\mathrm{SASCA}$ targeting masked secure multiplication, investigate the more computationally expensive variant in which a single factor graph is extended whenever a new measurement is added. Existing experiments instead decode a separate factor graph for each measurement and then recombine the resulting probabilities, with belief-propagation performance tending to worsen as noise increases. Determine the extended-graph variant's attack performance, particularly whether its gain over standard $\mathrm{DPA}$ is independent of noise, as previously observed for such attacks against an unprotected $\mathrm{AES}$ implementation.

scope.domain: Side-channel cryptanalysis of masked secure multiplication using SASCA with belief-propagation factor graphs.
parameters: Noise level, whose effect on attack performance and relative gain over standard DPA is under study
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the extended-factor-graph variant's attack performance, especially whether its gain over standard DPA is independent of noise.

citations.label: Masking Proofs Are Tight and How to Exploit it in Security Evaluations

progress.summary: The source reports that efficient per-measurement factor-graph decoding tends to perform worse as noise increases. It explicitly leaves the more expensive graph-extension variant open, motivated by noise-independent gains previously observed against unprotected AES.
citation_labels: Vincent Grosso et al., Masking Proofs Are Tight and How to Exploit it in Security Evaluations
